apparatus_caveat: The transcriptions preserve edition-specific e/ae and presbiter/presbyter, with abbreviation expansion, long-s, u/v, i/j, case, punctuation, accents and line layout treated as declared in each artifact. Lexical agreement under those declared normalizations does not establish substantive prayer revision. The 1804 title identifies a new printing of the Cisneros book, but does not identify the immediate exemplar of this blessing. Neither bibliographic succession nor changed printed placement establishes direct 1500-to-1804 textual parentage or the date of relocation. No Git parent, inheritance, complete Ordinary or whole missal is claimed.
basis: Both identified printings carry the complete source-defined Benedictio panis, with the same heading, opening dialogue, Benedic Domine prayer, blessing and final sprinkling rubric. All nine ordered semantic units are independently collated. In the 1500 witness the blessing follows the final index and precedes the colophon; in 1804 it appears among preliminary blessings on p. XVI. The comparison aligns the complete blessing constituents, not the surrounding books.

left.joined_source_text:
Benedictio panis. ℣. Adiutorium nostrum in nomine Domini.
℟. Qui fecit celum et terram.
℣. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.
℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in seculum.
℣. Domine exaudi orationem meam.
℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat. Dicat presbiter. Dominus sit semper vobiscum.
℟. Et cum spiritu tuo. Oremus.
Oratio. Benedic Domine creaturam istam panis: sicut benedixisti quinque panes in deserto: ut omnes qui ex eo gustaverint: tam corporis quam anime recipiant sanitatem. Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum. Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus. Per omnia semper secula seculorum.
℟. Amen. Dicat presbiter. Dominus sit semper vobiscum.
Respondeat chorus. Et cum spiritu tuo. Benedictio. Benedictio Dei Patris omnipotentis ✠ et Filii ✠ et Spiritus San✠cti descendat et maneat super hanc creaturam panis.
℟. Amen. Et statim aspergat aquam benedictam.
